text:
natalie: quick heads-up — our TLS posture scan this morning flagged a subset of service-to-service traffic in eu-west still negotiating TLS1.2. i'm proposing we enforce min TLS1.3 for east/west traffic and require mTLS for all internal services. also want to lock down cert private keys in KMS/HSM and surface cert serials in audit logs. who's got bandwidth to help scope? cc @mike @raj

mike: +1 on TLS1.3 everywhere as a target. caveat: some 3rd-party connectors in eu-west are stuck on older runtimes. we should plan per-route/region overrides for a short TTL before hard-blocking. can we gate by LB/proxy instead of touching every service?

raj: agree with proxy-first approach. suggested steps:
- add policy in ingress/envoy to set min_protocol = TLSv1_3 for internal clusters.
- deploy a passive monitor for 48h that logs TLS version + certificate serial on handshake, no deny.
- RBAC change: only security-oncall + infra-admins can approve any forced deny PRs. we should record approvals in audit logs.

raj: for KMS integration: store private keys in KMS (CloudHSM/KMS) and use signing API to do TLS handshakes where supported, otherwise use short-lived certs minted by a CA whose key is in HSM. audit log fields to add:
```
{
  "timestamp": "...",
  "service": "svc-name",
  "peer": "svc-other.eu-west-1",
  "tls_version": "TLS1.3",
  "cipher": "TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384",
  "cert_serial": "AB:CD:12:34",
  "kms_key_id": "projects/.../keyRings/.../cryptoKeys/...",
  "action": "handshake_success"
}
```

infra-bot: NOTICE: new CVE published: CVE-2026-1234 affects openssl < 3.2.2. Remediation: upgrade or apply patch. Affected hosts found in eu-west-k8s-nodepool-3. Ticket: SEC-2987.

julie: ++ on rolling canary and sdk fallback. DevEx can add a handshake error helper in our SDKs so product teams get clearer errors instead of generic connection failure. suggest adding a retriable error code when upgrade is required so apps can show maintenance notices gracefully.

sonya: if we flip enforcement we need a runbook snippet for incident responders. i'll paste a trimmed playbook: 
1) If services fail to handshake, check recent audit log entries for cert_serial + kms_key_id.
2) Run `openssl s_client -connect svc:443 -servername svc -tls1_3` to confirm negotiation.
3) If CVE symptoms observed, isolate nodepool and rotate workload to patched pool.
4) Escalate to infra oncall; if it's a cert mismatch, roll back proxy policy to 'monitor' for the region.

raj: envoy config example for min TLS version (canary):
```
transport_socket
  name: envoy.transport_sockets.tls
  typed_config:
    "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.transport_sockets.tls.v3.UpstreamTlsContext
    common_tls_context:
      tls_params:
        tls_minimum_protocol_version: TLSv1_3
```

mike: RBAC change idea: create a short-lived permit label `tls-enforce:region` applied by infra-admins. PRs that change enforcement must include an approvals checklist and link to a monitoring dashboard showing <1% TLS1.2 usage for 72h.

natalie: ok action items:
- raj to open an aggregate monitoring dashboard + add cert_serial logging (SEC-2990)
- mike to prototype proxy-level enforcement + region override (ENG-4123)
- julie to add SDK handshake helper + UX guidance (DX-987)
- sonya to update incident playbook and runbook snippets (ONCALL-75)
- infra-bot ticket SEC-2987 for OpenSSL upgrade — triage owners: infra + eng-runtime

natalie: timeline: monitor-only for 48h, canary enforcement in one region next week, full roll week after if metrics look good. anyone object?

mike: no objections. :thumbsup:

raj: will start the dashboard and KMS proof-of-concept. tagging infra for HSM policy input.

sonya: i'll draft the emergency rollback steps and test the s_client quickcheck in staging.

julie: i'll publish SDK helper and a short PR template for teams to report TLS failures.

natalie: thanks — i'll own comms to product/security channels and schedule a 30m sync if needed. :white_check_mark:
